units.translation: d. σφωιτέρους: he used σφωιτέρους incorrectly; for he should have said σφετέρους. But he meant 'he beheld the house' in the sense of 'he saw his own home in his mind'.
Schn.) they said; and he says that she is a she-dragon, called in the feminine Delphyna, as Callimachus himself says.

to be king, who because of his enmity towards the Bebryces and Amycus received the Argonauts hospitably. They say that he was the son of Dascylus son of Tantalus and of Anthemoeisia daughter of Lycus the river, as Nymphis also testifies in the first book of his Heraclea (fr. 5 M. III 13) and Herodorus
In the land of the Tibareni, when women give birth, they take care of their husbands, as Nymphodorus says in his Customs (fr. 15 M. II 379).
1160. γνωτοί: meaning 'kinsmen'. LgP
1162. Aeolus, Cretheus, Athamas, Aeson, Phrixus, Jason, Argus. Lm (P)

1172. στιάων: στιαι are what pebbles are called among the Sicyonians; so the hearth and the altar were constructed from pebbles. Or στιαι are the pebbles 〈that are from rivers, which are now called κόχλακες〉. Callimachus (Hymn I 26): 'πολύστιόν τε Μετώπην'.

6 Et. Gen. (AB) στεῖαι καὶ στειάων: as in II 1172. στεῖαι are what pebbles are called among the Sicyonians. So the hearth and the altar were constructed from pebbles. Or στεῖαι are the pebbles [καὶ deleted by Miller] that are from rivers, which are now called κόχλακες.
7 ἢ στῖαι αἱ ψ. with the rest supplied from Et. by Deicke 52 : στῖαι δὲ αἱ ψ. in L : omitted in P
9 Μετώπην in Call. : μέτωπον
1176. ἐπηετανὸν κομέουσαι: carefully and for a long time nourishing. LmP
1177. ἐπαρτέα: ready. LgP
1179. The speech is addressed to Argus, son of Phrixus, and he says: help us to bring the fleece to Greece. Lm(P)

1186. εἴτε μετὰ Φθίην: some say that Phthia is mentioned as a city of Orchomenus — 'Phthia, city of Orchomenus' — inasmuch as the Orchomenians are colonists of the Thessalians. But it could also refer to Orchomenus on the border of Macedonia and Thessaly. For there is an Orchomenus that is both a mountain and a city in Thessaly, Boeotia, Arcadia, and Pontus.
1189. κείνην: in which the sons of Phrixus were. LgSm(P)
1193. ἐπίρροθοι ἄμμι πέλ〈εσθε〉: ἐπιρροθεῖν properly means to urge on dogs. It also means to assist a ship, from ῥόθιον, which is the wave.
21 ἐπιρροθεῖν in this place in P : the same after κυσὶν in L
22 [καὶ deleted by W] κελ- in L : ἐπικελ- καὶ ἐρεθίζειν in P; σημαίνει δὲ in P : omitted in L
23 P adds at the end: here he simply calls the helper ἐπίρροθον. cf. W 42
1194-95. Ζηνὸς χόλ〈ον〉: because the divinity was angry with the descendants of Aeolus, since Phrixus had been in danger. Jason said this because Pelias also used such a pretext in sending him out.
25 Pind. Pyth. IV 281 with sch.
25 Ἰάσων in W : Ἀπολλώνιος
1196. ἔστυγον: they shuddered, they were afraid. LgGgSmP
